axes.name: Proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.assessment: Public documentation, code-diff and release inspection are labeled research; helper reveal and native activation are process steps. Product configuration, scans, offline operation, label generation and endpoint checks are consistently PROPOSED / NOT_RUN. No prototype is required. Proposed identity/foreign-key, explicit-confirm, idempotent replay, interruption/conflict, keyboard/terminator, damaged-label replacement, care/privacy/redirect and selected-version tests have meaningful expected observations. Product/server/event state must be the receipt oracle; decoding a payload is only a reader oracle; following a URL proves neither receipt nor offline durability. Migration checks apply only to the selected engine/parser path. Legacy-permissive FieldParser output must be compared with intended current-versus-legacy policy, not treated as blanket standards certification. No candidate local executable product witness is present or claimed.

material_findings.classification: materially incomplete governing source conditions / unsupported categorical product-fit limitation
material_findings.title: Snipe-IT default QR destination is treated as the built-in capability boundary
material_findings.candidate_claim: Its built-in QR leads to the private asset page, not the public care page.
material_findings.independent_finding: The rolling Asset Labels page describes an in-system QR path, but the release actually discussed, v8.8.0 (2c466fa8a5a68525439bf1bbbc24470d6670c516), exposes configurable 2D content and a prefix explicitly described as supporting an external URL. In app/View/Label.php, plain_asset_tag content is the escaped configured prefix concatenated with the asset tag, whereas hardware_id/default selects the internal asset route. The UI labels the hardware route as the default and offers the plain target separately. Thus the documented default is not the complete built-in QR capability boundary.
material_findings.materiality: The proposal uses the private destination as a fit distinction for one of its two principal workflow candidates in research specifically requiring investigation of the optional public crate-care QR. Omitting the released configurable external URL path can misdirect the reader toward excluding that integrated label path or adding a separate label-generation mechanism. This publicly answerable exception belongs in the product comparison even though selection, ownership, deployment, and validation legitimately remain open.
material_findings.conditions_and_limits: New Label Engine; selected template must support 2D output; QRCODE must be selected rather than none/null; use a supported plain target with an approved prefix and compatible tag grammar. The implementation HTML-escapes the prefix, so this is not proof of arbitrary URL/query compatibility. A prefix plus tag can form a public URL; a cooperative-owned endpoint, redirects, privacy, phones, and actual printed output remain NOT_RUN/UNKNOWN. Nothing here asserts an existing care page or requires selecting Snipe-IT. The final retains the public QR option overall; the finding concerns a material product-specific capability exception, not total scope erasure.
material_findings.charitable_reading: The statement is true for the default path described in the rolling docs. The final does not identify its private-page statement as only that default or disclose the released external-prefix exception, and the source conditions repeat the restricted account. This makes it a material incomplete comparison rather than merely a missing exhaustive catalogue entry.
